contract: One recorded pure pattern cycle and ordinary dispatcher per host Unit/Run: shared sealed request charge, the binding of each action chosen by its action kind and, for a schema map, its schema ID, schema/identity/committed host gate/Budget/authority/Approval checks, occurrence-first settlement, a nested callable's first admitted finish given to its parent, durable owner composition and explicit fail-stop recovery; charge exhaustion stops generation while retaining prior within-cap obligations, without new work or resend permission; `input/4`, `control/4` and `status/1` each wait for the engine at most 60,000 ms.
limits: Host provides authenticated correlation/current authority, checked pure prompt patterns/bindings/schemas (for each schema map a binding for every action schema that a pattern of the Run asks for under that kind, whose `result` is the schema that the pattern reads; each action schema in `schemas`; the same `bindings` on each restart), exclusive matching Store/Lease construction, ordinary supervision, clocks/wakes, capacity, outcome sink and physical fencing/outstanding-write confirmation before recovery. Byte caps are not a sandbox.

No model/tool/Lua dependency, recipe loader, child Run, outside-event action, cluster ownership, scheduler, hot configuration, implicit reopen, retry/rearm/reset or later-wave capability. One Run stream belongs exclusively to RunApprovalRelease; old Run remains unchanged.

Payload JSON <=65536 bytes/depth32; ingress <=262144; complete record/output <=16777216; control <=2097152 with future settlement/receipt reservations; slot <=131072, 64 active/256 lifetime occurrences; request map <=4456448; checkpoint <=33554432 including model, retained IDs, full replay witnesses and framing. Complete encoded bounds are authoritative; no truncation or borrowed future settlement capacity.

A binding is chosen by action kind and, for a schema map entry, by `schema_id` alone: two versions of one schema ID under one kind share one binding, a schema map has no default entry so an unmapped schema is refused as `missing_binding`, and bindings are fixed for the Run so a changed schema map is an incompatible restart. A nested child still finishes with the `result` of the binding chosen for its parent's action; a wrapper for another child schema belongs to the host. A `local_work` binding gives its `result` at version 1.

A nested finish reaches the parent only when its `{schema_id, schema_version}` equals the binding `result`, else the parent fails as `nested_result_invalid`; no finish keeps `nested_completed`. Only the first admitted finish counts; the payload is recipe content within the payload bounds, uninterpreted and not in `status/1`; it is dropped from durable control state once the parent action settles.

Request cap 1..256 is sealed per Run, shared with nested callables and never replenished by Attempt, pause/continue or restart. First excess creates only charge/stop bookkeeping, not actions/verdicts/outcomes/joins or a pattern input. Room rollover is explicit after prior terminal obligations settle; lifetime-action capacity is not reset.

`input/4`, `control/4` and `status/1` use one fixed call limit of 60,000 ms and take no limit operand or option; `status/1` replies only after an input that the engine is working on. An input at the bounds (64 active/256 lifetime actions) took about 4.2 to 5.0 s in 10 runs alone and 10 beside the Piece suite on a shared worker host, mostly in the journal write path of the owners below this Piece: one observation, not a time bound. A caller that needs a shorter wait runs the call in a process of its own and gives up the wait there (`Task.async/1`, `Task.yield/2`, `Task.shutdown/2`). When a call ends by the limit or its caller stops waiting, the exit says nothing about whether the input was applied and the engine goes on with it; the Contract states only the existing retry rule (the same ID again, never another; applied/duplicate means committed; changed bytes are a conflict) and no other way to learn the outcome or bound on the continued work.

FIFO DU input retention does not bound retained log/witness memory or recovery time. Full retained history is required for audit; pruned/damaged/incompatible history errors. Oversize checkpoint refuses nonfatally; no perpetual checkpoint guarantee.

Finite disposable-PostgreSQL/counting-fake-provider evidence, not production monitoring, universal proof, exactly-once external effects or physical no-send/cancellation. Unknown cost is not zero; Budget estimates do not enforce provider charges. Reserved intents/lost raw sink values never authorize resend.

grounding.claim: The 13 published named groups exercise recorded non-agent publication, charge/retained obligations, gate order/first verdict/restart, append rejection/uncertainty, reused occurrences/read-only audit, ASK/resource release, intent recovery, persistent Budget/nesting, Attempt routing, local recovery/cancel, lifecycle, resource consumption/cleanup and encoded bounds; the eight groups nested_result_reaches_parent, nested_result_wrong_schema, nested_without_finish, nested_result_bounds, nested_result_survives_restart, first_finish_only, two_levels and payload_not_exposed exercise the nested finish result, the group call_waits_past_the_default (test every_call_waits: an input that sleeps 5,500 ms once in the gate returns applied, and status/1 and control/4 sent during it each reply after it, more than 5,000 ms after they were sent) exercises the 60,000 ms call limit, the seven groups binding_by_schema, outcome_schema_by_binding, unbound_schema_refused, nested_binding_by_schema, person_and_authority_by_schema, restart_keeps_choice and effect_bindings_override exercise the binding chosen by schema ID and the test helper override effect_bindings, all with real ready APIs and disposable PostgreSQL. Temporary actual production gate/first-settlement bypasses, the old nested_completed outcome for a finished child (nested_result_reaches_parent fails) and a skipped result-schema comparison (nested_result_wrong_schema fails), a schema map that gives the binding of its first key whatever the action schema (binding_by_schema fails) and an outcome expectation read from the kind alone (outcome_schema_by_binding fails) are negative controls, as is the default 5,000 ms call limit (call_waits_past_the_default ends with the time-out exit); listed finite scenarios, not quantified proofs.
Pinned GenServer serialization, Registry/DynamicSupervisor and Task semantics compose ready owner Contracts; no local OTP runtime proof.
OTP29.1.2 deterministic minor-version-2 ETF/safe decoding and SHA-256 identities; full encoded bounds are checked, not inferred from JSON length.
Pinned compact JSON encoding/decoding retains admitted requests and originals; ready PayloadSchema owns JSON representation/depth/schema checks.

Host callbacks are prompt pure checked decisions where required, retain stable compatible identity/binding/schema bytes, authenticate people/results/current authority, serialize Run mutation with admission, preserve full durable history and fence old tasks/owners/providers. Fake observations and local PostgreSQL tests do not establish production fencing or vendor behavior. Reused Cure laws retain only their dependency-local scopes; no new engine proof or monitor is claimed.

telemetry.contract: OTP diagnostics only with redacted engine format_status; no custom telemetry, payload exporter or durable audit through observations.

config.contract: Fixed required host infrastructure, checked pattern/schema/gate/action bindings, explicit Run/period, request cap, monetary Budget, lifecycle rule/deadline and evidence Writer; compatible restart only, no defaults or hot replacement.

control.contract: Trusted stable-ID input and begin-Attempt/Approval evidence-revocation/pause/verified continue/targeted cancel through existing owners; committed status and explicit host recovery, no generic router/reset/rearm or physical cancellation promise.
